title: Held Up
logline: A long-distance bus breaks down on a rural road. Passengers step out into the heat with nowhere to be but exactly here, and the mood of the group shifts, more than once, before it moves again.

object.note: Object 3 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a workshop's slow, private tension to an hour of shared heat by a roadside: a broken-down bus and strangers whose mood shifts more than once.

thread_out.thread: The wait ends on the road but continues under a tree: farmers deciding together how a tank's water will be shared, and the moment arguing facts becomes arguing standing.

requirements: A rural long-distance bus route where the crew can travel and wait without arranging events
A genuine, unplanned breakdown occurring during the filming window
Consent from the driver, conductor and passengers involved

suggestions.name: A rural highway between provincial towns
suggestions.region: Uva Province, on the Passara–Monaragala road corridor
suggestions.why: A long hill-to-dry-zone route served by long-distance buses, offering real distance and time for a stop to matter to passengers.
suggestions.verify: This is a plausible route type, not a confirmed filming plan; a specific service and willing operator must be found.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Even a small, ordinary refusal, like a bus that will not move, can set off displeasure, and each person feels it inside before anyone else sees it. The texts name 'not getting what one wants' as one of the most common times this happens.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: බස් එක පාරේ කැඩී නවතිනවා වැනි පොඩි බාධාවකදී පවා ඇතිවන නොසතුට, අනුන්ට පෙනෙන්නටත් පෙර තමාගේම සිත තුළ දුකක් ලෙස දැනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Pradeepika lists the ordinary occasions when aversion arises, among them meeting what one dislikes and not getting what one wants, and Margaya adds everyday ones such as a request refused or a task not done. Both hate-rooted states always come with a painful mental feeling (domanassa), so the displeasure is suffering in itself. The texts also name restlessness (uddhacca), a mind that will not settle on its object and shakes like leaves in the wind, as present in every unwholesome moment.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film waits in real time with the passengers: the moment the engine dies, calls home, complaints to the conductor, fidgeting in the shade. The viewer can notice irritation rising and settling in different people at different times, and the shared water and small help that turn up in the same stalled crowd, without narration pointing at either.
lesson.caution: This does not mean that venting frustration clears it away; the texts treat this displeasure as painful in itself and offer no idea of discharging it safely by letting it out.
lesson.builds_on: The closed hand showed a slow, private holding back; here the same displeasure arrives quickly and in public, set off by nothing more than a road that will not let a crowd arrive.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
